title: 7th Sitting of second session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 and closed at 11:46. After routine business, the main item was the first debate on a bill to amend the law on becoming an islander of an island, brought by the North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim, which would let people who own land or property on another island register there without the current five-year residence period. MDP members spoke for it, saying the rule ties citizens to one island. PNC members spoke against it, saying the change is unnecessary or would draw people to the Malé region. In the vote the house declined to accept the bill, 12 for and 59 against. The attendance figure is read from garbled text and is uncertain.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Supported the amendment, saying people who own property or run businesses on an island should be able to register there.
Raised several points of order, saying the bill covers every island, not only the Malé region.
Argued the amendment text is clear and the house should accept it and refine it in committee.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Argued citizens should not be tied to one island and should have equal rights wherever they live.
Said unequal access to services and income between Malé and the islands comes from policy.
Responded to a point of order from the Central Maafannu member about flat allocation.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Opposed the amendment and criticised MDP members' remarks about Malé residents.
Said the government's land reclamation, including Rasmale, would address Malé's housing needs.
Disputed claims about land plots in Hulhumale'.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Introduced the bill so owners of land or property on an island can more easily register as islanders there instead of relying on five years' residence.
In closing, said differences between Malé and the islands exist and asked members to consider the changes.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Opposed the bill, saying it would draw more people to the Malé region.
Pointed to the President's plans for regional development and questioned the sponsors' motives.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Opposed the bill, saying he saw no purpose in the amendment and speaking of attachment to one's home island.
Responded on housing, citing flat numbers from 2013-2018 and 2018-2023 to dispute that MDP governments served Malé residents.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Opposed the bill, saying people can already change island registration easily.
Criticised past land allocations and said the proposal is not needed.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Opposed the bill, saying easier transfer of islander status is unsafe for a Muslim nation and raising identity concerns.
Said he would oppose the change to permanent address rules.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the bill only removes the five-year wait for changing island registration.
Argued that changing address does not remove a person's identity and urged PNC members to join the debate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said islanders can already change registration through local councils and questioned the proposal.
Used football teams signing players from other islands as an example of registration moves.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said people already move registration between islands and questioned why the change is needed; compared passport waiting times with other countries.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Argued that permanent-address rules tie people to one place and can cost them rights.
Said public money paid for reclaimed land in the Malé region.

speakers.name: Asma Rasheed
positions: Raised a point of order during the Hanimaadhoo member's speech; the chair said one member cannot answer another by point of order.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Opposed the amendment and said its aim is to make it easier to acquire land as areas are reclaimed.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Asked the sponsor to clarify the bill's reference to a fifth article, saying the law appeared to have only four.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Supported the amendment, saying people on islands lose rights under current laws and an MDP government would bring bigger change.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said very easy transfer of island registration could harm island communities and favoured a residence period of around five years.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Opposed the bill, arguing that a person's origin and island affiliation should not be erased and citing religious teachings.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the bill, saying current law causes hardship for citizens and members should not mock those seeking a legal fix.

Bill to amend Law 46/78 on becoming an islander not accepted: 12 for, 59 against.

votes.what: Accept the bill to amend Law 46/78 (becoming an islander of an island) for further consideration
